decisions.statement: A page type has its own properties and the properties of every type above that page type.
The nearest declaration binds.
A slug is looked for under every type descending from `page-type`.
The types descending from `page-type` are read once and held.
What one slug is looked up as is read once and held, a slug naming nothing too.
`page-type` is tried before every type descending from `page-type`.
Every declaration is answered as well as the binding declaration.
A property is keyed by the slug its own page states rather than by the slug the declaration names.
A declaration reaching no page property is left out rather than keyed by the declaration's name.
A record property declares its fields as a page type declares its properties.
A page type descending from a file property group declares that group's members.
A page of such a page type states none of those members.
Those members are answered apart from what the page type carries.
A field is declared by the record property with the field.
The declaration from the type named last binds where two are equally near.
A declaration stating a unique kind has that kind rather than its property's.
A declaration fixing a value is answered with that value beside it.
A page type that cannot be read is refused by name rather than answered as declaring nothing.
A refusal says a route of extending that reaches the type that cannot be read.
A reading answering nothing where a type cannot be read says so in its own name.
A page type listed at several paths is read from the listings that answer.
A listing opening nothing is no candidate.
Several listings with one id are answered as one page.
Several listings with different ids are answered as no page rather than settled here.
Nothing here judges the properties this module gathers.
Refusing two properties landing on one key is the check's work.
Nothing here walks the pages.

definition: the properties a page type or a record property carries, each under the key it is read by
